transcript:
Meeting: SDK & proxy alignment - Redwood x Zenith Labs
Date: 2026-11-09 14:00 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (Zenith CTO), Mina Park (Zenith Lead ML Eng), Samir Patel (Zenith Platform Eng)
---
[00:00] Alex Mercer: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, I'm Alex from Redwood, AE. Priya our solutions engineer is here.
[00:10] Carlos Vega: Hey all, Carlos here. we'll probably jump in on architecture and constraints.
[00:15] Mina Park: Mina. lead ml eng, we own model infra and prompt pipelines.
[00:19] Samir Patel: Samir, platform eng, we run the gateway and routing.
[00:24] Priya Nair: great. agenda — basic environment, SDK questions, gateway/proxy patterns, rate limits & quotas, observability hooks, and next steps. sound right?
[00:32] Carlos: yes. main ask — we need to pick between Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment; also want to understand how Redwood's SDKs and LangChain adapters will plug into our gateway mesh. we run Envoy + homegrown proxy.
[00:44] Alex: perfect. quick context check: what are your peak qps and latency SLOs for chat and batch embedding workloads?
[00:51] Mina: chat is typical 120 rps peak, 95th latency 350ms token-stream expected, embeddings batch jobs are nightly -> 2M rows in 3 hours. we also have strict data residency + SOC2.
[01:06] Priya: thanks. Those numbers point to either Dedicated or Private for predictable throughput and residency. Hosted can work if you want fast trial but we'd need Customer-managed VPC for Private. also mention KMS + audit logs for SOC2.
[01:22] Samir: on our side the gateway is critical — we do prefix-based routing, per-tenant quotas, and dynamic routing by region. we prefer a sidecar adapter or a proxy middleware rather than socket-level changes.
[01:35] Alex: Redwood SDKs have both HTTP and gRPC clients; we provide a lightweight proxy sidecar example + a connector for LangChain and LlamaIndex. our sidecar exposes a local endpoint that maps to per-tenant tokens, does prefix caching, and forwards to Redwood with mTLS.
[01:50] Mina: is that sidecar open source? can we run it inside our existing service mesh?
[01:54] Priya: the connector is MIT-licensed reference code; we provide Helm charts for k8s and an Envoy filter guide. it integrates with service meshes — you can run as sidecar or as central egress. most customers take the sidecar approach for tenant isolation.
[02:08] [02:08] (background) Speaker 1: mm-hmm
[02:12] Carlos: about LangChain — we use it heavily in orchestration. you mentioned adapter for LangChain. is it supported for async streaming and for LlamaIndex fetchers?
[02:22] Priya: yes, we've got a LangChain runtime adapter that supports streaming tokens via SSE and gRPC streaming. LlamaIndex we support via a built-in Retriever adapter and a small shim — though some index types need manual wiring. we can run a demo.
[02:38] Mina: any gotchas with KV cache and long-context models? our use-case uses 8k context and lots of repeated prefixes.
[02:46] Alex: runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching; you can configure cache TTL and pin prefixes per route. note: with Dedicated, we can tune kernel selection and batching aggressiveness — that reduces per-token cost.
[02:59] Samir: rate limiting — we have per-org quotas, burst allowances, and we want graceful 429 handling with backoff. how does Redwood expose quota data to the gateway?
[03:10] Priya: Redwood exposes token and request quota via a management API and also via headers in responses (X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining, X-Redwood-Rate-Limit-Reset). for real-time enforcement you can call the rate-check endpoint at 10 qps; for local enforcement we recommend leasing tokens to the sidecar to avoid round trips.
[03:28] Mina: and what about throttling penalties? we want deterministic latency rather than head-of-line blocking.
[03:34] Alex: we support prioritized routing: critical requests can use reserved capacity in Dedicated pools; fallback to cheaper model variants for best-effort requests, and client-side circuit-breaker recommendations.
[03:47] Carlos: security — SSO, SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS. can we bring our own KMS?
[03:54] Priya: yes for Private deployments you can integrate with your KMS/HSM. Hosted supports customer-managed keys via cloud KMS in select regions. we produce audit logs in JSON; retention and export options available.
[04:06] [04:06] Speaker 2: (inaudible)
[04:09] Samir: observability hooks — we need per-route latency histograms, token-level cost attribution, and traces across our gateway into Redwood.
[04:18] Alex: Console supports token-level cost breakdowns and per-model latency. for traces we instrument with OpenTelemetry; we provide tracing headers and examples for linking traces in Jaeger/Tempo. export of metrics via Prometheus is available for both Hosted and Dedicated.
[04:33] Mina: is telemetry sampled or full? we can't send PII upstream.
[04:37] Priya: telemetry is metadata-only by default; payloads are never captured for Hosted without explicit consent. for Private, you control everything. we can mask fields and filter spans at the sidecar.
[04:50] Carlos: about integration effort — our infra team estimates 3-4 sprints to adopt connectors and egress rules. what do you typically see?
[04:59] Alex: for a standard sidecar + LangChain adapter it's ~2-3 weeks for POC, including basic evals; full production (RBAC, KMS, SSO, audit) usualy 6-8 weeks.
[05:11] Mina: ok. now specifics: can the SDK sign requests with our short-lived tokens from our identity system? we want no persistent keys in apps.
[05:19] Priya: yes — we have a token-exchange flow. sidecar obtains short-lived credentials from your STS and uses them to mTLS to Redwood. keys rotated automatically.
[05:27] Samir: what about on-prem? we have some air-gapped GPU clusters for sensitive data. can Redwood run there?
[05:33] Alex: we support Private on-prem packages — control plane can be customer-managed and runtime runs in your cluster. there are additional ops and licensing terms; we'll share the on-prem checklist.
[05:44] [05:44] Carlos: let's talk about cost modeling a bit. how do we estimate per-token costs when using batching, caching, and Dedicated pools with reserved throughput?
[05:54] Priya: we provide an Optimize report that models token costs with parameters for average prompt tokens, average generated tokens, batching factor, cache hit rate. For Dedicated, you get an effective decrease in per-token cost due to sustained utilization and kernel tuning. we'll run a spreadsheet if you give us traffic profile.
[06:10] Mina: we will. also, we want guardrails — ability to force model variants per route and a safety layer for hallucination detection.
[06:19] Alex: rollouts and policy controls exist: you can pin routes to models, do canary percentages, and run quality monitors bound to prompt sets; automatic fallback policies can route to a safer smaller model for high-risk requests.
[06:33] Samir: is there a webhook or event stream for QA alerts?
[06:37] Priya: yes alerts can hit a webhook and also integrate with Slack, PagerDuty; we can push evaluation diffs with context to your S3.
[06:45] Carlos: our primary blockers are: legal sign-off for Hosted data flows, validating throughput for embeddings, and integrating with our Envoy mesh without rewriting much.
[06:55] Alex: action items we'll capture. We'll share the legal/security doc pack for Hosted and the on-prem checklist. For throughput we can run a bench with a small dataset and a Dedicated pilot or a Hosted stress test through your gateway.
[07:08] Mina: On the LangChain/LlamaIndex side — we use LlamaIndex DocStore heavily. does your adapter support incremental index updates and chunked retrieval?
[07:19] Priya: yes, we support chunked retrieval patterns and can stream partial index fetches. the shim for LlamaIndex will need a couple custom connectors for your storage backend — we can pair program on that.
[07:32] [07:32] Speaker 3: yep
[07:34] Samir: ENV specifics — we run EKS 1.28, Envoy 1.30, terraforms modules. do you have Helm charts and Terraform modules?
[07:43] Alex: Helm charts + example Terraform for control plane are available. we also have a small CLI to bootstrap sidecar configs and generate Envoy filter snippets.
[07:55] Carlos: any limitations around model families? we have internal fine-tuned models and plan to use open-checkpoint ones. will Redwood host our FT models on Dedicated?
[08:04] Priya: yes — Dedicated supports customer model onboarding; we provide quantization and runtime tuning assistance. for Private you can host fully on-prem. Lighter weight model variants are available as fallbacks.
[08:16] Mina: timeline — legal wants the security pack by Friday. can we get that by EOD Thursday?
[08:22] Alex: we can push a redlined security overview and the on-prem checklist by Thursday EOD.
[08:26] Carlos: perfect. last — what's the best way to validate integration with minimal risk?
[08:30] Priya: start with Hosted proof-of-concept through a dev namespace with a sidecar proxy that forwards from your Envoy; run a small prompt set, gather latency + token-cost, then move to a short Dedicated pilot if traffic and residency require.
[08:45] Alex: recap next steps and i'll drop the links in the follow-up: security pack (redwood.secure/zenith-docs link placeholder), Dedicated pricing sheet (link), LangChain demo repo (github.com/redwood-inference/langchain-adapter placeholder).
[09:01] Mina: sounds good. thank you all.
[09:05] Carlos: thanks.
---
